intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Knobloch syndrome-2 (KNO2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the PAK2 gene (605022) on chromosome 3q29.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 (KNO2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the PAK2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.

checks.claim: The PAK2 gene is located on chromosome 3q29.
checks.evidence_quote: Dominant monoallelic variant in the PAK2 gene causes Knobloch syndrome type 2.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, not stated in abstract but acceptable as restatement.

paragraphs.text: Menzel et al. (2004) described Knobloch syndrome as characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele. Wilson et al. (1998) noted that the cranial defect ranged from occipital encephalocele to a very mild scalp defect. Antonarakis et al. (2021) concluded that Knobloch syndrome-2 is a dominant form caused by a variant in the PAK2 gene.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome is characterized by high myopia.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists high myopia as a defining feature.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome is characterized by vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome is characterized by congenital encephalocele.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.

checks.claim: In Knobloch syndrome, the cranial defect ranges from occipital encephalocele to a very mild scalp defect.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on two sibs with high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration (VRD), and occipital encephalocoele or scalp lesion.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes two affected sibs. The cranial lesion was an occipital encephalocele or a scalp lesion, and one sib had a 'very mild scalp defect' ('the other is notable for the very mild scalp defect'). That fits the stated range, from occipital encephalocele to a very mild scalp defect. The observation comes from only two sibs, but the draft attributes it to Wilson et al. as something they noted, which is accurate.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 is a dominant form of Knobloch syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 is caused by a variant in the PAK2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.

paragraphs.text: Antonarakis et al. (2021) concluded that Knobloch syndrome-2 in the family they studied was dominant. The heterozygous PAK2 variant was apparently de novo in both affected sibs, which suggested germline mosaicism in one of the parents.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 in the family studied by Antonarakis et al. (2021) was dominant.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant

checks.claim: The heterozygous PAK2 variant in the Knobloch syndrome-2 family was apparently de novo in both affected sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings

checks.claim: The occurrence of the apparently de novo PAK2 variant in both affected sibs suggested germline mosaicism in one of the parents.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings indicating a likely germ-line mosaicism in one of the parents

paragraphs.text: Menzel et al. (2004) confirmed that Knobloch syndrome-1 (KNO1), an autosomal recessive form, is caused by mutation in the COL18A1 gene.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-1 (KNO1) is an autosomal recessive form of Knobloch syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: The abstract calls KNO autosomal recessive. It does not use the label 'KNO1', but naming the second locus KNO2 implies the COL18A1 form is the first.

checks.claim: Menzel et al. (2004) confirmed that Knobloch syndrome-1 is caused by mutation in the COL18A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of two unrelated KNO families from Hungary and New Zealand allowed us to confirm the involvement of COL18A1 in the pathogenesis of KNO and to demonstrate the existence of genetic heterogeneity.
checks.explanation: The authors confirmed COL18A1 involvement, having found two COL18A1 mutations in the Hungarian family.

paragraphs.text: Antonarakis et al. (2021) studied a family with Knobloch syndrome that was not linked to COL18A1. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous missense mutation in the PAK2 gene. The mutation was present in both affected sibs and was apparently de novo, because it was absent from their unaffected parents. In transfected HEK293T cells, the mutation caused a partial loss of PAK2 kinase activity.

checks.claim: Antonarakis et al. (2021) studied a family with Knobloch syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied an historical pedigree (published in 1998) designated as KNO2 (Knobloch type 2 syndrome with intellectual disability, autistic behavior, retinal degeneration, encephalocele).

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome in the family studied by Antonarakis et al. (2021) was not linked to COL18A1.
checks.evidence_quote: However, there are patients clinically diagnosed as Knobloch syndrome with unknown molecular etiology not linked to COL18A1. We studied an historical pedigree (published in 1998) designated as KNO2
checks.explanation: The abstract implies, but does not explicitly state, that this family was not linked to COL18A1.

checks.claim: Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous missense mutation in the PAK2 gene in the Knobloch syndrome family studied by Antonarakis et al. (2021).
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing of the two affected siblings and the normal parents resulted in the identification of a PAK2 non-synonymous substitution p.(Glu435Lys) as a causative variant. The variant was monoallelic

checks.claim: The PAK2 missense mutation was present in both affected sibs of the Knobloch syndrome family.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings

checks.claim: The PAK2 missense mutation was absent from the unaffected parents of the Knobloch syndrome sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings indicating a likely germ-line mosaicism in one of the parents; the mosaicism, however, could not be observed after deep sequencing of blood parental DNA.
checks.explanation: Apparently de novo after parental sequencing implies absence in parents.

checks.claim: The PAK2 missense mutation in the Knobloch syndrome sibs was apparently de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings

checks.claim: In transfected HEK293T cells, the Knobloch syndrome-associated PAK2 missense mutation caused a partial loss of PAK2 kinase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: Functional analysis of the p.(Glu435Lys) PAK2 variant in transfected HEK293T cells results in a partial loss of the kinase activity.
